routing: gpt_image_2 (quality medium, 1k, 16:9) for count-heavy orthographic sheets; flux_2 pro (1k, 16:9) for mood/hero frames; tripo_h3_1_image_to_3d (texture on, pbr off, face_limit 20000, orientation align_image) for proportion maquettes
sheet_prompt_template:
Production turnaround sheet for a low-poly racing game asset, three true orthographic views on one wide image: FRONT (left), SIDE (centre), TOP (right), exactly the same metre scale, front and side on a shared ground baseline. Flat neutral grey background, soft even studio lighting, no perspective, no ground shadow, no text except the small view labels and a 1 m scale bar. Complete asset in every view with enough spacing and no cropping.
ASSET: <name, overall metres, EXACT counts of every part, placement of each part>
ROLE IN THE RACE: <what the driver must read from it and at what distance>
STORY WEAR: <twenty years of humid weathering: rust streaks under bolts, sun-bleached top faces, algae at the base, one welded repair plate, faded stencil>
STYLE: remembered early-2000s console racer, original design, honest low-poly geometry, hand-painted texture language readable at 256-512 px, painted ambient occlusion, restrained palette of grey concrete, rust red, off-white, olive steel, sodium amber, swamp green.
AVOID: any real space-agency vehicle, any real logo, neon, photoreal PBR, bloom, tiny greebles, new details invented between views. Counts and proportions agree in every view.
hero_prompt_template: Ascension Pad, a racing circuit through a working rocket launch complex in a humid jungle estuary, for a remembered early-2000s console anti-gravity racer. Chase-camera view 2.4 m above a 24 m wide concrete racing road <where>, <the asset described exactly as in its sheet>, sodium lamps, mist, tropical overcast dawn with one warm break. Yellow-black hazard kerbs, painted worn lane markings, damp stained concrete. Painted hand-textured surfaces, honest low-poly geometry, restrained palette of grey concrete, rust steel, sodium amber, swamp green and mist, fog for depth, no bloom, no lens flare, no neon, no photoreal PBR, no vehicles.
division_of_labour: Higgsfield (FLUX.2 heroes, Tripo maquettes) is run by the orchestrator, not Codex. Codex has GPT Image 2 only and uses it for every remaining sheet and material-ID pass. Where no hero exists for a secondary asset, Codex makes it with GPT Image 2 using hero_prompt_template.
